title: Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability
abstract: arXiv:2611.24669v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. We introduce Movie2Game-Bench (M2G-bench), a benchmark for evaluating film-to-game adaptation beyond playability. M2G-bench combines general evaluation, movie-specific evaluation, and playtesting by three GUI model players. The protocol connects source content to gameplay steps and implementation evidence, capturing both content preservation and interactive realization. The benchmark comprises 22 films and 658 source-specific reference items. Evaluating 14 models on the same films with their selected primary harnesses reveals complementary strengths in game quality, adaptation, and player experience. A shared weakness concerns playable sequences: this category has the lowest content-presence mean in all 14 models, averaging 37.9 out of 100 compared with 54.8 for iconic elements. translated_title: Movie2Game-Bench：超越可玩性的电影到游戏改编整体评估
translated_abstract: 将一部电影改编成游戏，需要选择源素材并将其转化为玩家动作、规则和反馈。我们提出了Movie2Game-Bench（M2G-bench），这是一个超越可玩性层面、用于评估电影到游戏改编效果的基准。M2G-bench 结合了通用评估、电影专属评估以及由三个GUI模型玩家进行的试玩测试。该评估协议将源内容与游戏玩法步骤及实现证据相连接，同时捕捉内容的保留程度与交互的实现效果。该基准包含22部电影和658个源专属参考条目。在相同的电影上，使用各模型选定的主要测试框架对14个模型进行评估，结果显示它们在游戏质量、改编效果和玩家体验方面各具互补优势。一个共同的弱点体现在可玩序列上：该类别在所有14个模型中内容存在度均值最低，平均为37.9分（满分100分），而标志性元素的均值为54.8分。在关于被保留情感的判断中
tldr: 该论文提出Movie2Game-Bench基准，通过结合通用评估、电影专属评估和GUI模型玩家试玩测试，在22部电影和658个参考条目上对14个模型进行电影到游戏改编的整体评估，发现所有模型普遍在可玩序列的内容保留方面表现最弱。
en_tdlr: Introduces Movie2Game-Bench, a benchmark that holistically evaluates film-to-game adaptation beyond playability by combining general evaluation, movie-specific evaluation, and GUI model player playtesting across 22 films and 658 reference items, revealing a shared weakness in content preservation of playable sequences among all 14 evaluated models.
